templates.title: BentoPDF
templates.name: bentopdf
templates.description: PDF toolkit that runs in your browser, so files never leave your machine. Merge, split, compress, convert, sign and edit. Source: https://github.com/alam00000/bentopdf
templates.note: Open http://<your-host>:8090. There's no login and nothing to back up, since every PDF is processed in your browser rather than on the server. Converting Word, Excel or PowerPoint files needs it served over HTTPS though (or opened as localhost on the same machine), as browsers block the bit it relies on over plain http. Docs: github.com/alam00000/bentopdf

templates.title: ConvertX
templates.name: convertx
templates.description: File converter for over a thousand formats, covering images, documents, audio, video and ebooks. Source: https://github.com/C4illin/ConvertX

env.name: HTTP_ALLOWED
env.label: Opening it over plain http?
env.description: ConvertX only sends its login cookie over HTTPS unless this is on. Switch it off once it's behind a reverse proxy with HTTPS.

templates.note: Open http://<your-host>:3000 and create your account straight away, since the first visitor gets it and sign-ups close after that. Uploads and the database live in the /app/data volume. It's a big image (LibreOffice, TeX and Calibre are all in there), so the first pull takes a while. You'll be logged out whenever the container restarts, unless you add a JWT_SECRET env var holding a long random string (openssl rand -hex 32). Docs: github.com/C4illin/ConvertX

templates.title: CyberChef
templates.name: cyberchef
templates.description: Web app for encoding, decoding, encrypting, compressing and picking apart data, by chaining hundreds of small operations into a recipe. Source: https://github.com/gchq/CyberChef
templates.note: Open http://<your-host>:8088. There's no login and nothing to back up, since every recipe runs in your browser and your data never reaches the server. Recipes live in the URL, so bookmark or share that to keep one. Docs: github.com/gchq/CyberChef/wiki

templates.title: Etherpad
templates.name: etherpad
templates.description: Collaborative text editor where everyone types in the same document at once, with history, chat and plugins. This one runs on Postgres. Source: https://github.com/ether/etherpad

env.name: ETHERPAD_ADMIN_PASSWORD
env.label: Admin password (required)
env.description: For the admin panel at /admin, where you sign in as admin. Generate one with: openssl rand -hex 32

env.name: ETHERPAD_DB_PASSWORD
env.label: Database password (required)
env.description: Generate one with: openssl rand -hex 32. Keep it the same when you redeploy, or Etherpad can't reach its database.

env.name: ETHERPAD_PORT
env.label: Host port for the web UI

templates.note: Set both passwords before you deploy (openssl rand -hex 32 makes good ones), since the stack won't start without them. Then open http://<your-host>:9001 (or whichever port you picked) and start a pad. Anyone who can reach it can create and edit pads, so keep it off the open internet or put a login in front of it. The admin panel is at /admin, user admin. Pads are stored in Postgres, in the postgres-data volume. Docs: docs.etherpad.org

templates.title: RSSHub
templates.name: rsshub
templates.description: RSS feed maker for thousands of sites that don't have a feed of their own, like GitHub issues, news sites, forums and shops. Source: https://github.com/DIYgod/RSSHub

env.name: ACCESS_KEY
env.label: Access key
env.description: Optional. Set one and every feed url needs it, like /hackernews?key=yourkey. Leave blank and anyone who can reach it can use it.

templates.note: Open http://<your-host>:1200 to check it's up, then add feeds to your reader as paths on it, like /github/issue/DIYgod/RSSHub. Every route is listed in the docs. There's no login, so set an access key if it faces the internet. Nothing to back up, feeds are cached in memory. Some routes need a browser, and for those swap the image tag to chromium-bundled.

templates.title: Seerr
templates.name: seerr
templates.description: Request manager for Jellyfin, Plex and Emby, where people ask for films and shows and Sonarr and Radarr fetch them. It's the merged successor to Overseerr and Jellyseerr. Source: https://github.com/seerr-team/seerr
templates.note: Open http://<your-host>:5055 and the setup wizard walks you through connecting your media server, then Sonarr and Radarr. Settings and the request database live in the /app/config volume. Coming from Overseerr or Jellyseerr? Seerr can take over their config, see the docs for how.

templates.title: Super Productivity
templates.name: super-productivity
templates.description: To-do list with timeboxing and time tracking built in, and it can pull in issues from Jira, GitHub and GitLab. Source: https://github.com/super-productivity/super-productivity
templates.note: Open http://<your-host>:8095. There's no login, and your tasks are saved in your browser rather than on the server, so set up sync (WebDAV, Dropbox and others) in its settings if you use more than one device. Docs: github.com/super-productivity/super-productivity

templates.title: Termix
templates.name: termix
templates.description: SSH terminal and server manager in the browser, with saved hosts, tunnels and a file editor. Source: https://github.com/Termix-SSH/Termix
templates.note: Open http://<your-host>:8080 and create an account, which becomes the admin. Registration stays open after that, so switch it off in the admin settings unless you want other people signing up. Hosts, keys and the database live in the /app/data volume, and its secrets are generated there on first start. Behind a reverse proxy it needs websockets. It sends a small anonymous usage report once a day, which you can switch off in Admin Settings > Usage Statistics. Docs: docs.termix.site

templates.title: Wallos
templates.name: wallos
templates.description: Subscription tracker for keeping an eye on recurring bills, with stats, multiple currencies and reminders before things renew. Source: https://github.com/ellite/wallos

env.name: TZ
env.label: Timezone
env.description: Like Europe/London. Used for renewal dates and reminders.

templates.note: Open http://<your-host>:8282 and register. The first account becomes the admin, and sign-ups are closed after that. The database and any logos you upload live in the two volumes. Docs: github.com/ellite/wallos
